record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.original_question: If negative-norm physical states are admitted in string theory on AdS3, can they be interpreted consistently by identifying the instability they represent and its physical origin in the AdS3 background, and can the known non-unitary models based on admissible SU(1,1) current-algebra representations be understood within string theory?

evidence.quote: a somewhat more exotic attitude with respect to the unitarity could be to simply admit the presence of negative-norm states in the physical spectrum, and then try to interpret them or, better, to identify the instability they are related to and its physical origin within the ADS3 background.

Following this line of thought, one could even reconsider the – non-unitary – models based on the admissible representations of the SU(1,1) current algebra; their partition function is known, and one should then try to understand them in the framework of string theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider bosonic string theory whose target space includes an AdS₃ factor, realized via the SL(2,ℝ) (equivalently SU(1,1)) WZW model at level k. The chiral algebra is the affine ŝu(1,1)_k current algebra, whose representations include: (i) the principal continuous series, (ii) the highest/lowest weight discrete series 𝒟⁺_j and 𝒟⁻_j, and (iii) the "admissible" representations of Kac–Wakimoto, which exist for fractional levels k+2 = p/q with p,q coprime positive integers and which possess modular-invariant characters but are non-unitary as representations of su(1,1).

(a) Suppose one drops the usual no-ghost requirement and admits negative-norm physical states in the string spectrum on AdS₃. Provide a consistent physical interpretation of such states: identify the dynamical instability of the AdS₃ background (or of the string propagating in it) that these negative-norm states would signal, and explain its physical origin.

(b) The non-unitary conformal field theories built from the admissible ŝu(1,1)_k representations admit known modular-invariant partition functions. Determine whether and how these admissible-representation models can be incorporated as consistent backgrounds for string theory on AdS₃, including a description of the resulting physical (BRST-cohomology) spectrum, its spacetime interpretation, and the role of the negative-norm states arising from the non-unitarity of the admissible representations.
artifact.category_tag: AdS3 string theory and SL(2,R) WZW representations
artifact.status_search_result: After the landmark works of Maldacena–Ooguri on the SL(2,ℝ) WZW model, the physical spectrum of strings on AdS₃ is now built from unitary discrete (with j<k/2) and continuous representations plus their spectral-flow images, and ghosts decouple. Modular invariants based on admissible (non-unitary) representations have been constructed, but a consistent string-theoretic interpretation of admitting negative-norm states or of using admissible-representation backgrounds—including identifying the precise instability they encode—does not appear to have been definitively established in the literature; the question remains essentially open/unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model, Part 1
status_evidence.snippet: Hilbert space consists of continuous and discrete representations and their spectral flow; no-ghost theorem requires j<k/2.
status_evidence.claim: The accepted unitary spectrum uses j<k/2 discrete plus continuous reps and their spectral flows; admissible reps are not part of this spectrum.

status_evidence.title: Modular invariance of string theory on AdS3
status_evidence.snippet: Modular invariants for admissible representations exist only for k<2 and require infinitely large spins.
status_evidence.claim: Modular-invariant partition functions for admissible SU(1,1) representations are known but their string-theoretic meaning is unsettled.

status_evidence.title: AdS3 Integrability, Tensionless Limits, and Deformations: A Review (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of AdS3 string spectrum focuses on unitary discrete and continuous representations; admissible representations are not used.
status_evidence.claim: Recent reviews do not report a resolution incorporating admissible non-unitary representations into AdS3 string theory.
